lecture.New_Day9Part1audio01.mp3: Welcome to Day 9! Today, we master SQL's ultimate branching tool: the CASE expression. In data analytics, raw database rows rarely match business categories. CASE gives you the power to categorize data, handle edge cases, and pivot metrics directly inside your queries.
lecture.New_Day9Part1audio02.mp3: The CASE expression is SQL's equivalent of an IF-THEN-ELSE structure. It evaluates conditions sequentially and returns the result of the first matching condition. If no condition evaluates to true, it returns the value specified in the ELSE clause.
lecture.New_Day9Part1audio03.mp3: SQL supports two CASE formats: Searched CASE and Simple CASE. Searched CASE uses boolean expressions like WHEN salary greater than 80000. Simple CASE tests a single variable against discrete equality targets.
lecture.New_Day9Part1audio04.mp3: Searched CASE is far more flexible and commonly used in production because it supports ranges, inequalities, AND, OR, and NULL checks.
lecture.New_Day9Part1audio05.mp3: In Query 1, we categorize employee salaries into four distinct bands: Executive, Senior, Mid-Level, and Junior. Notice how the conditions are arranged in descending numerical order.
lecture.New_Day9Part1audio06.mp3: Ordering matters in CASE statements! Because SQL evaluates WHEN clauses from top to bottom and stops at the very first match, placing broad conditions before narrow ones can cause severe logic bugs.
lecture.New_Day9Part1audio07.mp3: Simple CASE evaluates a single expression once, matching against specific values. It is ideal for code-to-description lookups, such as expanding status codes or department abbreviations.
lecture.New_Day9Part1audio08.mp3: In Query 2, we map order status codes into human-friendly business terminology: Shipped becomes Fulfilled, and Processing becomes In Progress.
lecture.New_Day9Part1audio09.mp3: One of SQL's most potent patterns is Conditional Aggregation. By wrapping CASE inside aggregate functions like SUM and COUNT, you can pivot multiple categorical metrics into side-by-side columns in a single table pass.
lecture.New_Day9Part1audio10.mp3: In Query 3, we count shipped orders versus processing orders side-by-side, avoiding slow subqueries or separate table scans.
lecture.New_Day9Part1audio11.mp3: Handling NULLs in CASE statements requires special attention. Always provide an explicit ELSE clause. If you omit ELSE and no conditions match, SQL silently returns NULL.
lecture.New_Day9Part1audio12.mp3: CASE is also invaluable for preventing runtime errors like division by zero. By checking if the denominator equals zero, you can safely return NULL or zero instead of crashing.
lecture.New_Day9Part1audio13.mp3: Did you know you can use CASE expressions inside ORDER BY? This enables custom sorting orders that alphabetical or numerical sorting cannot achieve.
lecture.New_Day9Part1audio14.mp3: In Query 4, we prioritize orders by custom business urgency: Processing orders appear first, followed by Shipped orders, without altering the underlying data.
lecture.New_Day9Part1audio15.mp3: Cross-database parity: CASE is ANSI-standard SQL and works identically across SQLite, PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, Snowflake, and BigQuery.
lecture.New_Day9Part1audio16.mp3: You're now fully prepared to leverage conditional logic! Let's jump into the practice lab and solve high-impact retail analytics challenges.

questions.New_Day9Question01.mp3: Salary tier classification! From employees, return first name, salary, and a calculated salary tier: Executive for salaries 100000 or more, Senior for 75000 or more, Mid-Level for 50000 or more, and Junior for anything below.
questions.New_Day9Question01sol.mp3: Let's classify salaries into tiers. SELECT first name, salary, CASE WHEN salary >= 100000 THEN Executive WHEN salary >= 75000 THEN Senior WHEN salary >= 50000 THEN Mid-Level ELSE Junior END AS salary tier... FROM employees.
questions.New_Day9Question02.mp3: Order value segmentation! From orders, return order ID, customer ID, total amount, and order size: Small for amounts under 2000, Medium for amounts under 15000, and Large for amounts 15000 and above.
questions.New_Day9Question02sol.mp3: Let's segment orders. SELECT order ID, customer ID, total amount, CASE WHEN total amount < 2000 THEN Small WHEN total amount < 15000 THEN Medium ELSE Large END AS order size... FROM orders.
questions.New_Day9Question03.mp3: Customer tenure cohort! From customers, return first name, signup date, and customer status: Veteran if signed up before 2023-01-01, otherwise Recent.
questions.New_Day9Question03sol.mp3: Let's flag veteran customers. SELECT first name, signup date, CASE WHEN signup date < 2023-01-01 THEN Veteran ELSE Recent END AS customer status... FROM customers.
questions.New_Day9Question04.mp3: Translate order status codes! From orders, return order ID, status, and status label: Completed Order when status is Shipped, In Flight when status is Processing, and Pending Review otherwise.
questions.New_Day9Question04sol.mp3: Let's label order statuses. SELECT order ID, status, CASE status WHEN Shipped THEN Completed Order WHEN Processing THEN In Flight ELSE Pending Review END AS status label... FROM orders.
questions.New_Day9Question05.mp3: Inventory replenishment alert! From products, return name, stock quantity, and inventory status: Critical if stock is under 20 units, Moderate if under 50 units, and Plentiful otherwise.
questions.New_Day9Question05sol.mp3: Let's classify stock levels. SELECT name, stock quantity, CASE WHEN stock quantity < 20 THEN Critical WHEN stock quantity < 50 THEN Moderate ELSE Plentiful END AS inventory status... FROM products.
questions.New_Day9Question06.mp3: Conditional order counts! Count total orders, completed orders where status equals Shipped, and pending orders where status equals Processing across the orders table.
questions.New_Day9Question06sol.mp3: Let's count orders conditionally. SELECT COUNT star AS total orders, COUNT of CASE WHEN status = Shipped THEN 1 END AS shipped count, COUNT of CASE WHEN status = Processing THEN 1 END AS processing count... FROM orders.
questions.New_Day9Question07.mp3: Calculate annual employee bonus! Return first name, salary, and projected bonus: 10 percent of salary if salary is below 60000, else 5 percent of salary.
questions.New_Day9Question07sol.mp3: Let's compute bonus amounts. SELECT first name, salary, CASE WHEN salary < 60000 THEN salary * 0.10 ELSE salary * 0.05 END AS bonus... FROM employees.
questions.New_Day9Question08.mp3: Safe profit margin calculation! From products, return name, unit price, cost price, and markup percentage calculated as unit price minus cost price divided by cost price multiplied by 100, returning 0 if cost price is 0.
questions.New_Day9Question08sol.mp3: Let's prevent division by zero. SELECT name, unit price, cost price, CASE WHEN cost price = 0 THEN 0.0 ELSE ROUND of unit price minus cost price times 100.0 divided by cost price, 2 END AS markup pct... FROM products.
questions.New_Day9Question09.mp3: Flag high-cost technical staff! From employees, return first name, department ID, salary, and compensation tier: High-Cost Tech if department ID is 10 or 20 and salary is 80000 or more, else Standard.
questions.New_Day9Question09sol.mp3: Let's evaluate multi-condition logic. SELECT first name, department ID, salary, CASE WHEN department ID IN 10, 20 AND salary >= 80000 THEN High-Cost Tech ELSE Standard END AS compensation tier... FROM employees.
questions.New_Day9Question10.mp3: Sort by custom business urgency! Return order ID, status, and total amount from orders, ordered so Processing orders appear before Shipped orders.
questions.New_Day9Question10sol.mp3: Let's sort with CASE. SELECT order ID, status, total amount... FROM orders... ORDER BY CASE status WHEN Processing THEN 1 WHEN Shipped THEN 2 ELSE 3 END, total amount DESC.
questions.New_Day9Question11.mp3: Product price tiering! From products, return name, unit price, and price category: Budget for prices under 1000, Standard for under 10000, and Luxury for 10000 and above.
questions.New_Day9Question11sol.mp3: Let's assign price categories. SELECT name, unit price, CASE WHEN unit price < 1000 THEN Budget WHEN unit price < 10000 THEN Standard ELSE Luxury END AS price category... FROM products.
questions.New_Day9Question12.mp3: Fiscal quarter mapping! From orders, return order ID, order date, and fiscal quarter: Q1 for months 01 through 03, Q2 for 04 through 06, Q3 for 07 through 09, and Q4 for 10 through 12.
questions.New_Day9Question12sol.mp3: Let's extract fiscal quarters. SELECT order ID, order date, CASE WHEN strftime percent m comma order date IN 01, 02, 03 THEN Q1 WHEN strftime percent m comma order date IN 04, 05, 06 THEN Q2 WHEN strftime percent m comma order date IN 07, 08, 09 THEN Q3 ELSE Q4 END AS quarter... FROM orders.
questions.New_Day9Question13.mp3: Audit commission compensation! From employees, return first name, commission, and commission status: Eligible if commission is not null, otherwise Base Salary Only.
questions.New_Day9Question13sol.mp3: Let's check commission status. SELECT first name, commission, CASE WHEN commission IS NOT NULL THEN Eligible ELSE Base Salary Only END AS commission status... FROM employees.
questions.New_Day9Question14.mp3: VIP order indicator! From orders, return order ID, customer ID, total amount, and VIP flag: VIP Order if total amount is 50000 or greater, otherwise Regular Order.
questions.New_Day9Question14sol.mp3: Let's flag high-value orders. SELECT order ID, customer ID, total amount, CASE WHEN total amount >= 50000 THEN VIP Order ELSE Regular Order END AS vip flag... FROM orders.
questions.New_Day9Question15.mp3: Multi-metric revenue breakdown! Calculate total revenue from Shipped orders and total revenue from Processing orders in a single summary row using conditional aggregation.
questions.New_Day9Question15sol.mp3: Let's pivot revenue by status. SELECT SUM of CASE WHEN status = Shipped THEN total amount ELSE 0 END AS shipped revenue, SUM of CASE WHEN status = Processing THEN total amount ELSE 0 END AS processing revenue... FROM orders.
